title: Meet Paige, PagerDuty’s SRE Agent: Faster Fixes Today, Fewer Incidents Tomorrow by PagerDuty
summary: Paige, the PagerDuty SRE Agent, detects, triages, and helps resolve incidents so your best engineers can sleep through the night. See how Paige works.
body_markdown:
Today, we’re introducing Paige,


[PagerDuty’s SRE Agent](https://www.pagerduty.com/platform/ai-agents/sre/) . Built on over 16 years of operational data, Paige works as a member of operations, engineering, and DevOps teams, coordinating signal intelligence, incident management, and automation.


Paige learns from every incident, so every incident improves the next response. Each resolution is written back into shared memory, making every response sharper than the last. Knowledge that used to live only in responders’ heads becomes organizational intelligence that compounds over time.


With AI agents generating code at record speed and more of that code running in live, customer-facing environments, your team needs knowledge that grows as fast as your systems do.


Teams are feeling the burn.


[Forty-two percent of organizations cited developer burnout](https://www.pagerduty.com/state-of-ai-first-operations/) as a direct effect of major incidents. Your best engineers are bogged down with toil. They have no time left to improve your operations system or build your product roadmap. They rarely get a chance to get a good night’s sleep.


Those same engineers are the ones your systems depend on most. Paige is here to work alongside them. Paige depends on their expertise, too. The challenge is that data about the current incident, as well as past incidents, is scattered across spreadsheets, communications channels, and people’s heads. It rarely makes it to a comprehensive post-incident review that is well-documented and ready for future use.


As part of the


[PD Reliability Platform](https://www.pagerduty.com/platform) , Paige operates alongside you to detect, remediate, and prevent incidents. By learning from your team at every stage of the incident lifecycle, Paige keeps systems running, often stopping incidents before customers ever notice, without leaning on the same few people every time.


It’s time to let your engineers build, innovate, and get more sleep.


##### **The 3 a.m. page, reimagined**


It’s 3 a.m. You know how this goes:


- **A slow start:** Your engineers scramble through telemetry to find the problem.


- **A derailed call:** You join the call with your team. Latecomers keep asking, “What’s going on?” Each question pulls the discussion back to the beginning.


- **A long remediation:** Once someone finds the cause, fixing it takes another hour.


- **Lost lessons:** The post-incident review gets filed away, and no one reads it again.


Then everyone tries to get back to sleep before the workday starts again.


With Paige:


- **Teams start faster:** Consolidate alerts and telemetry into one clear picture and automatically connect the right team.


- **Meetings stay focused:** Post a quick summary and answer questions for late joiners, so no one has to interrupt the meeting.


- **Engineers resolve incidents faster:** Test competing hypotheses, suggest fixes based on your data and similar past incidents, and show the reasoning behind them. With your permission, Paige can even resolve well-understood incidents.


- **Resilience improves with every incident:** Draft your post-incident review, so you have more time for deep analysis. Each resolution adds to shared memory, making your team and systems more resilient.


Paige works inside the tools your team already uses, with 750+ integrations including Slack, Microsoft Teams, and more. Putting an AI agent in the middle of your incident path might feel risky, but Paige never goes beyond the boundaries you set. You define exactly what Paige can see, do, and act on.


##### **What Paige can do**


Paige is always on call, investigating alerts and events before they become incidents. As a virtual responder in your escalation policy, Paige orchestrates a team of supporting agents when needed:


- **Scribe Agent** keeps important records.


- **Shift Agent** runs the schedule.


- **Insights Agent** surfaces proactive recommendations.


Let Paige coordinate, so your responders can focus on the incident.


###### **Detect early and cut the noise**


Paige pulls in telemetry signals, so fewer issues slip through.


- **Catch emerging issues:** Spot disruptions early, often before your team notices.


- **Work across your stack:** Read signals from across your observability tools, and connect through MCP to Claude and Cursor for custom setups.


- **Pull it all together:** Combine telemetry and alerts from Signal Intelligence with context from past incidents into one triaged view for responders.


Let Paige remove the noise, so your responders can get to work.


###### **Triage, diagnose, and show the work**


You don’t have to dig through documentation, half-asleep, to find who owns an incident. Paige rallies the right team automatically.


- **Route incidents:** Use prior incident data and documentation to classify incidents and find the right owners.


- **Brief the team:** Post a summary of the event, tailored to each stakeholder, before they join. Responders can start work immediately, reducing


[mean time to resolution (MTTR)](https://www.pagerduty.com/resources/devops/learn/what-is-mttr/) .


- **Weigh hypotheses:** In Deep Investigation, a PD Labs experiment in preview, Paige tests several root causes at once, ranks them by confidence, and shows what was ruled out and why.


- **Narrate the reasoning:** Show each step along the way, so you can see how Paige reached an answer and decide whether it holds up. In the incident channel, a post might read: “Ruling out the DB failover. Timestamps don’t line up. Deploy still the leading cause.”


- **Investigate together:** In SRE Workbench, an experiment now in preview in PD Labs, your team and Paige work from the same data to dig into complex incidents.


You decide what happens next: investigate further, apply Paige’s suggested resolution, or take another path. When multiple incidents hit at once, you also decide which to act on first.


###### **Resolve known incidents, suggest fixes for new ones**


While your team works on a solution, Paige suggests resolutions based on what worked in similar past incidents, adapted to the situation at hand.


- **Take action:** Run specific runbooks where available, such as restarting services or running Kubernetes remediation, across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments.


- **Apply on approval:** Apply an approved resolution and report back on whether it worked.


- **Resolve autonomously (coming soon):** Handle well-understood incidents you define without waking the on-call team.


You’re always in control: Your team sets what Paige can see and do for each user group.


###### **Keep it from happening again**


Once the incident is resolved, Paige posts the findings right away.


- **Draft the review:** Start the post-incident review immediately, so your team can spend time on deeper analysis instead of assembling timelines and copy-pasting logs.


- **Learn across incidents:** Read Jira tickets, telemetry, and Slack conversations for each event to identify patterns. Every resolution and correction sharpens the next response.


- **Shift left:** Connect to Claude or Cursor through MCP to flag risks in your development environment before code ships. If a pull request resembles a change that caused a past incident, or could break a downstream service, Paige warns your team so they can fix it first.


Every incident makes the next one less likely, and easier to handle when it comes.


##### **What does Paige need to drive impact in your organization?**


You control what Paige can see and do by configuring three areas: authority, data, and feedback.


###### **Human-in-the-loop authority**


No matter how good Paige gets at resolving incidents, some decisions should stay with your team. You decide the threshold for automation.


Novel incidents often require human judgment, backed by senior engineers’ expertise in how your systems and dependencies behave. And while Paige can draft messages to stakeholders, you and your team own the conversation with executives, customers, and each other.


Those judgment calls also feed back into Paige. Every human input becomes part of shared memory, so your team gets better support at every stage.


###### **Clear access to data**


Paige needs access to the same resources your engineers use: telemetry, ownership mapping, escalation policies, runbooks, and your connected tools.


Organizations tend to make one of two mistakes when they bring in an AI agent:


- In a rush for results, they give an agent full system access but no ownership mapping, escalation policies, or runbooks. Without that context, the agent fills the gaps with assumptions instead of your team’s expertise.


- Hesitant to trust AI, they give an agent limited data and assign it only to narrow tasks. Without enough context or scope, your team ends up doing the work the agent was supposed to take off their plate.


The right setup gives Paige full context, with permissions aligned with your team’s comfort level.


###### **Feedback as Paige learns**


Every organization works differently, so Paige needs time to learn your processes. Paige shows the reasoning behind every step, and when your team corrects or redirects a response, that input sharpens the next one. Every incident teaches Paige more about how your team operates.


We also invite your thoughts on what’s working and what’s not. If you have an idea for how Paige can work better for you, tell us. Your feedback shapes what comes next.


##### **Common questions about Paige**


###### **Does Paige take action or just make suggestions? Can my team override the recommendations?**


That depends on your configuration. Paige can execute approved workflows directly or surface recommendations for your team to run. Either way, your team remains in control.


You set the rules for what Paige acts on and what needs human approval, including whether any incidents can be resolved autonomously. You can override recommendations at any time.


###### **What if Paige is wrong?**


Every step comes with the reasoning and evidence behind it, so your team can catch or roll back a bad call before it becomes a problem. Corrections feed back into Paige, making the same mistake less likely next time.


###### **AI agents are unpredictable. How can we trust Paige with our whole backend?**


Paige operates only within the permissions you set, which define what can be seen and acted on. Every step is shown, so your team can verify the reasoning.


Reliability also improves with use: Every incident, decision, Slack thread, and post-incident review deepens Paige’s understanding of what your best engineers know by heart.


##### **Watch Paige work today.**


AI is shipping new code faster than ever, and your team needs an agent that can keep up. Paige helps resolve incidents faster and prevent the next ones.


Start with the incidents your team already knows how to fix, then decide when you’re ready for Paige to take on more.


Your best engineer doesn’t need to wake up at 3 a.m. for an incident Paige can handle. Your team needs their sleep, and their energy for the work ahead.


Meet Paige, PagerDuty’s SRE Agent: faster fixes today, fewer incidents tomorrow.


[Schedule a demo and watch Paige work](https://www.pagerduty.com/platform/paige/) .
